question: The "Keibul Lamjao National Park", the only floating national park in the world, is in______________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Keibul Lamjao National Park** is located in the state of **Manipur**, India. It is renowned as the **only floating national park in the world**.
 
• This unique park is situated on the **Loktak Lake**, which is the largest freshwater lake in northeastern India, known for its distinctive floating islands called **phumdis**.
 
• The park is home to the **Sangai deer**, also known as the **Brow-antlered deer**, which is the state animal of Manipur and is classified as **Endangered** by the IUCN.
 
• Keibul Lamjao National Park spans an area of approximately **40 square kilometers** and plays a crucial role in the conservation of the unique biodiversity of the region.
 
• It was declared a national park in **1977** to protect the habitat of the Sangai deer and the rich flora and fauna of the area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phumdis:**

 
 
• **Phumdis** are floating biomass consisting of a heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, and organic matter in various stages of decomposition.
 
• These floating islands are found only in Loktak Lake and provide a unique ecosystem for flora and fauna.
 
• The phumdis support the livelihood of locals who use them for fishing and other activities.
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake:**
 
 
• **Loktak Lake** is the largest freshwater lake in northeastern India and is often referred to as the **"Lifeline of Manipur"**.
 
• The lake plays a vital role in the socio-economic and ecological balance of the region, supporting agriculture, fishing, and hydropower generation.
 
• In 1990, Loktak Lake was designated as a **Ramsar site**, recognizing its international importance as a wetland.
 
 
 
• **Sangai Deer:**
 
 
• The **Sangai deer** is an endemic species found only in Manipur, primarily in Keibul Lamjao National Park.
 
• Known for its graceful movement, the deer is also called the **"Dancing Deer of Manipur"**.
 
• Conservation efforts are ongoing to protect this endangered species, which faces threats from habitat loss and poaching.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity of Keibul Lamjao National Park:**
 
 
• The park is home to diverse fauna, including species like **hog deer**, **otters**, **waterfowl**, and many migratory birds.
 
• It also harbors several rare aquatic plants and serves as a critical habitat for fish and other aquatic organisms.
 
• The park's unique ecosystem makes it an important area for ecological research and conservation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Significance:**

 
 
• Keibul Lamjao National Park is located on the southern shore of Loktak Lake, at an altitude of **768 meters above sea level**.
 
• Its unique floating habitat is critical for the survival of the Sangai deer and other endemic species.
 
 
 
• **Ecotourism Potential:**
 
 
• The park is a key destination for ecotourism, attracting visitors for its unique floating ecosystem and rich biodiversity.
 
• It provides opportunities for bird watching, boating, and exploring the cultural heritage of Manipur.
 
 
 
• **Threats and Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• The park faces threats from human activities, including encroachment, pollution, and changes in water levels due to hydropower projects.
 
• Conservation initiatives include community participation, awareness campaigns, and habitat restoration projects to ensure the sustainability of this unique ecosystem.
